conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
NEPHROLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 01/21/2022
Patient: Philip Hall, DOB 07/22/1956
Referred by: primary care, for rising serum creatinine

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for asking us to evaluate Mr. Hall, a 65-year-old retired postal worker with long-standing type 2 diabetes complicated by neuropathy and retinopathy, hypertension and hyperlipidemia, treated a year ago for vitamin B12 deficiency.

He tells us that for about two months he has felt increasingly worn out and gets short of breath walking uphill or carrying groceries. He has had no chest pain, no racing heartbeat and no fainting. No urinary complaints, no leg swelling. No NSAID use.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, insulin glargine 30 units at bedtime, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Allergies: none known.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Vegan diet.

Exam: BP 140/85, pulse 88, respirations 18. Comfortable at rest. Heart: regular rhythm, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear on both sides. No peripheral edema.

Labs drawn today: hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, creatinine 1.9 mg/dL, BUN 36 mg/dL, potassium 5.5 mEq/L. Prior urine albumin/creatinine ratios from your office have not been elevated.

Impression:
1. Chronic kidney disease stage G3b, most consistent with diabetic and hypertensive kidney disease, non-albuminuric pattern. Creatinine has risen steadily over three years.
2. Mild hyperkalemia, 5.5, on an ACE inhibitor with a high-potassium plant-based diet.
3. Anemia, now microcytic (it was macrocytic during his B12 deficiency last year). Iron deficiency is the leading concern and could explain his fatigue and exertional breathlessness. Would appreciate your evaluation with iron studies.

Recommendations:
- Continue lisinopril 20 mg for now.
- Met with our renal dietitian today: lower-potassium choices within a vegan diet (portion limits on potatoes, tomatoes, bananas, beans; leaching technique for root vegetables).
- Repeat BMP in 1-2 weeks; can be drawn at your office.
- Avoid NSAIDs and IV contrast without prophylaxis.
- Return to nephrology in 12 months with labs, sooner for potassium over 5.8 or creatinine over 2.3.

We appreciate the referral.

Nephrology

events.reason: Fatigue, short of breath on exertion; nephrology follow-up

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 84. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. No ST or T-wave changes. No prior tracing for comparison.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: Fatigue, Anemia, CKD
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his nephrology consult last week; letter reviewed.

HPI: Two to three months of fatigue and getting winded on hills and stairs. Not as bad as last winter, he says, but clearly there. No chest pressure, no palpitations, no orthopnea, no ankle swelling. No black or bloody stools, no other bleeding. Appetite fine. Still strict vegan; B12 shots monthly at home on schedule. Last CBC here in August was 12.6 with MCV 86; at nephrology hemoglobin 9.8 with MCV 72.

Exam: pale conjunctivae. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Abdomen soft, nontender. Neuro unchanged.

ECG today: normal sinus rhythm, no ischemic changes.

A/P:
1. Microcytic anemia, new since August, after B12 replacement. Suspect iron deficiency (iron-poor diet, plus a big jump in red cell production once the B12 was replaced). Iron studies today. He has never had a colonoscopy, FITs negative 2018 and 2019. Will refer to GI if iron is low.
2. Exertional dyspnea and fatigue: ECG normal, lungs clear, no signs of heart failure; most likely the anemia. Will recheck symptoms once treated.
3. CKD 3b (new from nephrology): potassium recheck today per their plan, dietitian advice reviewed. Continue lisinopril.
4. DM2: A1c due in spring.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with vitamin C-rich food, not with tea

orders.reason: Iron deficiency anemia; no prior colonoscopy

documents.title: Results: Iron Deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt. Ferritin 7, transferrin saturation 5%: iron deficiency. Potassium down to 5.0 on the diet changes; creatinine 1.86, stable.

Plan: ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, take with orange juice or fruit, away from tea/coffee; may darken stools and constipate. Diet alone unlikely to correct this. Because he is 65 and has never had a colonoscopy, referring to GI for colonoscopy as part of the workup. He agreed this time. CBC in about 3 months.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ENDOSCOPY CENTER: COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Procedure date: 03/22/2022
Patient: Philip Hall, 65 M
Indication: iron deficiency anemia; no prior colonoscopy; maternal grandfather with colon cancer.
Allergies: NKDA.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care with propofol. ASA class III.
Prep: split-dose PEG, excellent throughout.

Findings: digital rectal exam normal. The scope was advanced to the cecum, confirmed by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve; terminal ileum intubated and normal. Withdrawal time 11 minutes. No polyps, masses, angioectasias or colitis. Normal retroflexion in the rectum. No blood seen.

Impression: normal colonoscopy to the terminal ileum. No colonic source of iron deficiency.

Recommendations:
- Continue oral iron per PCP. If iron deficiency does not correct on oral iron, upper endoscopy would be the next step.
- Repeat colonoscopy for screening in 10 years.
- Resume prior diet and medications.

Gastroenterology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: Iron Deficiency, Diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Taking iron daily, some constipation, managing with prunes. Energy better; he can walk the hill to the mailbox cluster without stopping now. Colonoscopy in March was normal, report reviewed. B12 shots continue.

O: color improved. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: skin intact, no ulcers, sensation as before.

CBC: Hgb 11.9 (from 9.8 in January), MCV 79. A1c 9.1.

A/P:
1. Iron deficiency anemia, responding to oral iron. Continue ferrous sulfate. CBC at the August wellness visit, then ferritin when he finishes ~9-12 months.
2. DM2, A1c 9.1. Offered once more to adjust glargine or add an agent; he declines for now, wants to concentrate on getting his energy back. Continue current regimen.
3. CKD 3b: BMP in August.
RTC August, annual wellness.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare annual wellness visit.

Updates: colonoscopy 3/2022 normal, repeat 2032. Nephrology 1/2022, CKD 3b, follow-up there in January. Iron deficiency on oral iron, energy back. B12 monthly at home.

Functional: independent in ADLs and IADLs, drives days only. No falls. Hearing fine for conversation. Walks most mornings. Health care proxy (wife) form returned and scanned.
PHQ-2: 0. Cognition: no concerns from him or wife, recall 3/3.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM monthly, ferrous sulfate 325 daily. NKDA.

Exam: well, BMI in the overweight range. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Feet: no wounds, monofilament reduced at toes, pulses palpable. 

Plan:
- Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine albumin, B12.
- Shingrix #1 today; #2 in 2-6 months, with flu shot and pneumococcal vaccine in October.
- Eye exam overdue (no 2022 exam yet); front desk to help him rebook.
- Personalized prevention plan printed.

documents.title: Wellness visit labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Philip,
Hemoglobin 13.2 - nearly back to normal, great to see. Keep taking the iron for now; we'll check your iron stores early next year and probably stop it then.
Kidney function stable, creatinine 1.83. Potassium normal now.
A1c 8.8, the best it has been since you joined, though still above goal.
B12 level good. Cholesterol fine.
See you in October for the shots.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Vaccines given after screening (no fever, no prior reactions):
- Influenza high-dose 0.7 mL IM L deltoid
- Shingrix dose 2, 0.5 mL IM R deltoid
- PCV20 0.5 mL IM R deltoid, separate site 1 inch apart
VIS sheets for all three. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction. Told to expect a sore arm and maybe a day of feeling tired after Shingrix. Plans COVID booster at the pharmacy next week. Eye appointment: patient says he will call them himself.

documents.title: Missed visit call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called re: missed appt 11/29. Spoke with wife; he forgot, they were at a family gathering out of town. Offered December dates, wife will check with him and call back. Left note for PCP.

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Re: Philip Hall, DOB 7/22/1956
Nephrology follow-up, 01/19/2023

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Hall returns one year after his initial visit. He feels much better; the fatigue and breathlessness he had last winter resolved as his iron deficiency was treated. He has kept to the lower-potassium food choices.

Medications: metformin, insulin glargine, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, oral iron, monthly B12 injections. NKDA.

BP today acceptable, no edema. Labs from 01/12: creatinine 1.82 mg/dL, potassium 4.9.

Assessment: CKD G3b, stable over the year; potassium now normal on lisinopril with diet changes.
Plan: continue current therapy, BMP with your routine labs, return in 12 months.

Nephrology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Missed the November visit (was out of town). Feels well. Nephrology in January: stable, letter reviewed. Still on daily iron, a year now. B12 monthly. Sugars "up and down" over the holidays, fasting 160s-240s. No lows. Feet: no new problems. Still hasn't rebooked the eye doctor.

O: vitals reviewed. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: intact, no calluses.

Labs back before he left: ferritin 64, A1c 9.4, CBC normal.

A/P
1. Iron deficiency anemia: resolved, stores repleted. Stop ferrous sulfate. CBC yearly.
2. DM2: A1c 9.4. Long talk. He understands the risk to his kidneys and eyes. Still declines insulin titration or a new agent; agrees to check fasting sugars daily for a month and send the log. Will revisit.
3. CKD 3b: stable per nephrology.
4. Eye exam: gave him the ophthalmology number again.
RTC May.

documents.title: stopping iron
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doctor, just to be sure, I can throw away the iron pills now? And I keep the B12 shots? Philip

documents.title: RE: stopping iron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, you can stop the iron pills. Please do keep the monthly B12 shots, those are long-term. And remember the fasting sugar log for the next month.

documents.title: RN outreach: missed visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after second missed diabetes visit in 6 months. Pt apologetic, says he mixed up the dates. Never sent the sugar log. Denies lows, no foot wounds, feels fine. Rebooked for 6/26 with text reminders turned on. Reinforced keeping the appointment given kidney function and A1c.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back after a missed visit in May. Checking sugars "most days" now, meter shows fasting mostly 150-210, a couple in the 240s. No lows. Walking in the mornings again. Eye exam is booked for July.

Exam: no distress. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet skin intact, no ulcers, reduced monofilament at toes as before.

A1c 9.2.

A/P: DM2 unchanged. We discussed once more; he prefers to keep the current regimen. I documented the risks and that the offer stands. Continue metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30. Lisinopril, atorvastatin continue.
RTC August for wellness visit.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Patient: Philip Hall, DOB 07/22/1956. Exam date 07/06/2023. Last seen here 06/2021.

VA cc 20/30 OD, 20/30 OS. IOP 16/17. Lenses clear for age. Dilated fundus exam with photos: diabetic retinopathy both eyes, no clear progression compared with 2021. OCT: no macular edema.

Assessment: diabetic retinopathy OU without macular edema, stable.
Plan: return 12 months. We stressed the importance of yearly exams given his long diabetes history.
NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, 67 y/o.

Since last year: iron stopped in February. Eye exam July, stable. Nephrology January, stable. Two missed visits this past year, both rebooked.

Function: independent; drives locally in daylight; manages his own pills, wife helps with the B12 shot. No falls. Hearing OK.
PHQ-2 0. Cognition: no concerns, 3/3 recall.
Activity: walks 3-4 mornings a week.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30 qhs, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM monthly. NKDA.

Exam: well-appearing. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses palpable, reduced monofilament and vibration at toes, unchanged.

Plan:
- Labs today (A1c was done in June).
- Flu shot in October; COVID updated vaccine at the pharmacy when available.
- Screening: colonoscopy 2022 normal. Vaccines otherwise up to date (Tdap 2018, PCV20 and Shingrix 2022).
- Diabetes: next A1c at fall visit.

documents.title: Your August labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Philip, labs from your wellness visit: blood count steady, so the iron stayed up after stopping the pills. Kidney function stable (creatinine 1.88). Cholesterol and urine protein fine. No changes needed. See you in the fall.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Flu Vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fluzone High-Dose 0.7 mL IM to left deltoid. No contraindications on screening. VIS provided. Tolerated without issue, left after 15 minutes. He'll get the COVID vaccine at his pharmacy.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, nocturnal incontinence

documents.title: Office Visit: Urinary Symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: hard to start urinating, and now wet at night.

HPI: 67M. For about a year it has been harder to get the stream going; it's slow, starts and stops, and he dribbles after he thinks he's done. Often feels he hasn't fully emptied. He put it down to age. In the last few weeks he has woken two or three times with wet underwear without knowing he'd gone, which upset him enough to call. No burning, no blood in the urine, no fever, no pain over the bladder. No new medications. No back injury, no new back pain, no leg weakness. Bowels regular.

Exam: abdomen soft, no tenderness; lower abdomen hard to assess fully, no obvious distension at the start of the visit. Genital exam normal. Prostate deferred to urology. Neuro: reduced sensation feet as before, ankle reflexes diminished.

UA negative. PSA 1.2, normal for age. BMP: creatinine 1.92, near his baseline. A1c 9.0 (drawn with the rest).

A/P:
1. Voiding symptoms with probable incomplete emptying and new night-time leakage in a man with long-standing diabetic neuropathy. Could be prostate-related, but a weak bladder from diabetic nerve damage is high on the list. Referring to urology for evaluation including a post-void residual. Caution with anything anticholinergic in the meantime.
2. DM2: A1c 9.0.
3. CKD 3b: stable.
Follow up after urology.

documents.title: Urology appointment and results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hello Mr. Hall, your urine test showed no infection and your PSA (prostate) blood test was normal. Your urology appointment is Friday January 19 at 1:40 pm. Please arrive with a comfortably full bladder; they will check how well it empties. Call us if the leaking gets worse or you cannot pass urine at all.
